summary: Frontend-only e2e test of the new 3-step deposit wizard on PHP+MariaDB DYNOVA NETWORK via FastAPI proxy. Signup → deposit wizard step1→2→3 → submit with screenshot → admin pending list → approve → balance credited. All happy-path checks PASS. Found 1 real UX bug: the Back button on Step 3 is blocked by HTML5 'required' validation on the TID input because the Back button lives inside the same form as the required field.

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking 'Back' on Step 3 ([data-testid='deposit-back-3']) does NOT navigate back to Step 2. The Back button is a submit button inside the same <form> that contains the REQUIRED transaction_id input ([data-testid='deposit-tid']). Browser HTML5 validation fires on submit and shows tooltip 'Please fill out this field', blocking the back action. Repro: open wizard, go to step 3 with empty TID, click Back — URL stays at step=3. Step-indicator-2 still has class 'step done' (i.e., $step is still 3).
ui_bugs.fix_hint: Add formnovalidate attribute to the Back button: <button type="submit" name="action" value="back" class="btn ghost" formnovalidate data-testid="deposit-back-3">. Same applies to deposit-submit only insofar as it should validate — but Back must bypass validation. (Step 2 Back is in its own separate <form> with no required inputs, so it works fine.)

issues: pm-account-number text content includes the trailing 'Copy' button label when extracted via textContent — minor: copy button could be moved outside the data-testid='pm-account-number' element so automated tests can read the raw number cleanly. Not a user-visible bug.

action_items: Add formnovalidate to the Step-3 Back button so users can return to Step 2 without first filling the required Transaction ID. File: /app/dynova/app/views/user/deposit.php, button [data-testid='deposit-back-3'].
critical_code_review_comments: deposit.php step-3: Back button shares the same <form> as required TID input → HTML5 validation hijacks the back navigation. Either (a) add formnovalidate to deposit-back-3, or (b) move the Back button into its own separate <form> like step-2 does. Option (a) is the smaller patch.

deposit.php step-2: pm-account-number testid wraps both the number text AND the 'Copy' button. Putting data-testid on the inner <span> with just the number would let automated tests assert the number value without string-cleaning.

WalletController::deposit step-3 submit branch: if screenshot save fails after Deposit::create() is reached, no rollback is attempted. Currently $errors short-circuits before create, so this is mostly fine, but consider wrapping the upload+create in a try/catch + transaction for robustness.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Signup form has 4 required text fields: name (optional), whatsapp, password, confirm, captcha. Forgetting 'confirm' makes the page bounce back to login silently. Captcha is plain integer addition. Admin login is at /api/?r=admin/login and uses input[name='email']. Container PHP/MariaDB freshly seeded so DB starts empty. The 3-step wizard uses PHP $_SESSION['dep_wizard'] keyed via the FastAPI-proxy session cookie — Playwright's default browser context preserves it across page.goto calls automatically.
rca_of_the_issue: Step-3 Back navigation bug RCA: In /app/dynova/app/views/user/deposit.php (lines 144–187) the entire Step-3 view is wrapped in a single <form enctype='multipart/form-data'>. Inside it, the Transaction ID input has the HTML attribute `required` (line 156). Both the Submit button (name=action value=submit) and the Back button (name=action value=back, [data-testid='deposit-back-3'], line 180) are type='submit' children of this form. When the user clicks Back with TID empty, the browser performs constraint validation on every submit button without formnovalidate, sees the empty required TID, focuses it and shows the 'Please fill out this field' tooltip, then aborts submission. The POST to the controller never happens, so the controller's `if ($action === 'back' && $step > 1) redirect(...)` branch is never hit. Mitigation: add `formnovalidate` to the Back button — it tells the browser to skip validation for that submit button only, while the Submit button continues to validate normally.
